messages.content: For a shopkeeper, make this a polite question: How much is this? Give a discount.
Excuse me, how much does this cost? Is there any chance of a small discount?

Plain English version, please. Sugriva is the Vanar king, and Rama has promised to help him.

Then glad was King Sugriva's breast,
And all his lords their joy confessed,
Stirred by sure hope of Rama's aid,
And promise which the prince had made.
Then King Sugriva was filled with joy, and all his lords showed their happiness too. They now had firm hope of Rama's help and of the promise the prince had made.

Use words a small child would know instead of "plonked", "whimper" and so on.

Liam's plush lion was on top of the toy chest in the Dublin flat, and he'd been hopping at it for ages. Finally he plonked onto the rug and gave a thin whimper. His eyes went round the room until they found Mum, Wanjiru, at the laptop. He toddled to her, grabbed her sleeve and pointed. "Lion." Wanjiru followed his finger, stood and handed it down. Liam hugged it hard.

Liam's soft toy lion was on top of the toy box in the Dublin flat, and he had been jumping up to reach it for a long time. At last he sat down on the rug with a small, sad cry. He looked around the room until he saw his mum, Wanjiru, at the laptop. He walked over, pulled her sleeve and pointed. "Lion." Wanjiru looked where he was pointing, stood up and got it down for him. Liam hugged it tight.
Rephrase this so a child can say it politely to her grandmother: Give me more rice. I'm still hungry.
Dadi, may I please have some more rice? I am still a little hungry.
Join these into one sentence using "because": Tanvi stayed home from the picnic. She had a bad cold.
Tanvi stayed home from the picnic because she had a bad cold.

Retell this from Reena's point of view, in the first person.

In the afternoon heat, Reena's goat wandered from the shed to the shade by the well. Reena watched her lie down. Soon Harish Bhaiya came up the lane with his school bag. "I'll give Chhoti her water in the shed," he said, picking up the bucket. Reena covered her mouth and giggled. "Bhaiya thinks she's in the shed!" she told Amma. "He didn't see her go." Then she ran after him. "Bhaiya, she's by the well!"

In the afternoon heat, my goat wandered from the shed to the shade by the well. I watched her lie down. Soon Harish Bhaiya came up the lane with his school bag. "I'll give Chhoti her water in the shed," he said, picking up the bucket. I covered my mouth and giggled. "Bhaiya thinks she's in the shed!" I told Amma. "He didn't see her go." Then I ran after him. "Bhaiya, she's by the well!"

Retell this from Binita's point of view, in the first person.

At her sixth birthday in the society clubhouse, the lights went off and everyone started singing. Shalini had been racing around with Binita all evening. Now twenty grown-ups and children stood in a ring around her, every face looking her way. The candles glowed. Shalini's cheeks went hot. She pulled her frock over her knees, ducked her head below the table edge and whispered, "Stop singing." Binita crouched beside her. "Blow fast and it finishes," she whispered back. Shalini blew, then hid her face in Binita's shoulder, grinning.

At Shalini's sixth birthday in the society clubhouse, the lights went off and everyone started singing. Shalini and I had been racing around all evening. Now twenty grown-ups and children stood in a ring around her, every face looking her way. The candles glowed. Her cheeks went hot. She pulled her frock over her knees, ducked her head below the table edge and whispered, "Stop singing." I crouched beside her. "Blow fast and it finishes," I whispered back. Shalini blew, then hid her face in my shoulder, grinning.

Use easier words and shorter sentences for this passage.

Monday: Tejas teased his sister Diya about her missing front tooth until she squealed. Wednesday: At the park, Hrithik from the next lane shoved Diya off the swing, and she landed on her hands. Tejas dropped his bat and ran. He stood in front of her and said, "Don't touch my sister." His voice shook, but his fists stayed open. He took Diya's hand, walked her home and told Papa what happened. Friday: Tejas was calling Diya "gap-tooth" again, but he gave her the bigger half of his biscuit while he did it.

On Monday, Tejas teased his sister Diya about her missing front tooth until she squealed. On Wednesday, Hrithik from the next lane pushed Diya off the swing at the park. She landed on her hands. Tejas dropped his bat and ran. He stood in front of her and said, "Don't touch my sister." His voice shook, but his fists stayed open. He took Diya's hand and walked her home. He told Papa what happened. On Friday, Tejas was calling Diya "gap-tooth" again. But he gave her the bigger half of his biscuit while he did it.

Turn this into two long sentences.

Monday: Jasleen stood under the shelf where her rag ball lay, stretched and fell on her bottom, cross.
Thursday: she pointed at the ball, turned to Nani on the charpai and said, "Uh, uh!" Nani laughed and lifted it down.
Sunday: Jasleen didn't stretch at all. She marched to Nani, patted her hand twice, pointed up and said, "Uh, uh." Nani's long arm went up, and the ball came down into Jasleen's waiting hands.

On Monday, Jasleen stretched for the rag ball on the shelf and fell on her bottom, cross; on Thursday she pointed at it and said "Uh, uh!" to Nani on the charpai, who laughed and lifted it down. On Sunday she did not stretch at all but marched to Nani, patted her hand twice, pointed up and said "Uh, uh," and Nani's long arm went up and the ball came down into her waiting hands.

Make this three sentences long and keep the main points.

Monday: At school in Madurai, Naveen argued fiercely in the class debate on whether homework should be banned, waving his hands and making everyone laugh. His teacher, Vasudha-ma'am, praised his sharp points.
Wednesday: At home, when his uncles discussed which college his cousin should choose, Naveen had an opinion, but he kept his eyes down and served the water. In their house, children listened when elders spoke.
The next Sunday: His grandfather asked him directly, "Naveen, what do you think?" Naveen hesitated, glanced at his father, then spoke softly and carefully, his debate voice tucked away but his point just as clear. His grandfather nodded, impressed.

Naveen argued fiercely in a class debate in Madurai and was praised by his teacher, Vasudha-ma'am, for his sharp points. At home he kept his eyes down and served the water while his uncles discussed which college his cousin should choose, because children listened when elders spoke. When his grandfather asked him directly what he thought, he spoke softly and carefully, and his grandfather nodded, impressed.
Ask it indirectly, beginning "Could you tell me": Where did Rahul put the keys?
Could you tell me where Rahul put the keys?

Squeeze this note into two sentences.

Evening note from Farida Nani, for Ayesha's Ammi
Today I opened the big black umbrella inside the verandah. Whoosh! Ayesha's eyes went round, her mouth made an 'O', and she fell back on her bottom. Then she laughed and laughed. I closed it and opened it six times, and each time she squealed and clapped. By the end she was pushing the button with me.

Farida Nani opened the big black umbrella inside the verandah, and Ayesha fell back on her bottom in surprise, then laughed. After Nani closed and opened it six times to squeals and claps, Ayesha was pushing the button with her.

Two sentences, no quotation marks: shorten this.

The power went out on a cold December evening.
"Where's Ankita?" Imran, her papa, whispered in the dark.
Ankita, fifteen months, giggled nervously.
He switched on the torch under his chin. "Boo!"
Ankita gasped, eyes huge, then laughed.
"Torch off. Where's Papa?"
Silence. Ankita patted the dark air.
"Torch on! Boo!"
She shrieked and grabbed his nose.
"Again?"
"Gain!"
By the time the lights came back, both of them were hoarse from laughing.

When the power went out one December evening, Imran played peekaboo with fifteen-month-old Ankita, switching his torch on and off and calling out boo each time. Ankita gasped, giggled, patted the dark air and shrieked with laughter, and by the time the lights came back, they were both hoarse from laughing.

What does this verse say? Write it in modern English prose.

He passed within, by Tara pressed,
And by his own impatient breast,
Refulgent there in sunlike sheen
Sugriva on his throne was seen.
Gay garlands round his neck were twined,
And Ruma by her lord recline.

He went inside, urged on by Tara and by his own impatient heart. There Sugriva was seen on his throne, shining with a light like the sun. Bright garlands were twined around his neck, and Ruma reclined by her lord.
Make this a friendly suggestion with "let's": You and I should practise cricket together.
Let's practise cricket together.
Change to the second person (use "you"): He waters his plants every day and talks to them.
You water your plants every day and talk to them.
Say this more casually: I am unable to join you for dinner this evening.
I can't join you for dinner tonight.

Shorten this text.

Yesterday my mother and I went to the market. We walked there slowly, because it was very hot. We bought some fruit and vegetables, and then we walked back home.
My mother and I walked slowly to the market yesterday because it was hot. We bought fruit and vegetables and walked home.
Rewrite in a casual tone: I am sorry to trouble you, but could you move your bag?
Sorry, could you move your bag?

Please make this text shorter.

The festival is on Friday. There will be music and dancing. Everyone in the village is going to be there, and all are welcome.
The festival is on Friday, with music and dancing. Everyone in the village is welcome.
